info.title: CanvasNet Tool
info.description: DemaConsulting.CanvasNet.Tool is the canvasnet command-line tool: it inspects, renders, and transforms images and documents (PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, JPEG 2000, SVG, PDF, PowerPoint, Visio, OpenSCAD models, Vega-Lite charts, and Mermaid diagrams) using the CanvasNet libraries, with a stable machine-readable JSON contract so that scripts and AI agents can drive it.

commands.name: compare
commands.description: Measure how much two images differ (MAE, RMSE, PSNR, SSIM), and draw the differences

options.name: --page
options.description: The page or slide to render, counted from 1 (default 1)

options.name: --dpi
options.description: Resolution of a PDF, PPTX, or VSDX page in dots per inch (default 96; VSDX needs a whole number)

options.name: --a-page
options.description: The page or slide of the first input, counted from 1 (a document only; overrides --page)

options.name: --b-page
options.description: The page or slide of the second input, counted from 1 (a document only; overrides --page)

options.name: --a-dpi
options.description: Resolution of the first input in dots per inch (a document only; overrides --dpi)

options.name: --b-dpi
options.description: Resolution of the second input in dots per inch (a document only; overrides --dpi)

options.name: --background
options.description: Opaque color that transparency is flattened over: white (default), black, #RRGGBB, or a color name

options.name: --no-auto-orient
options.description: Do not turn a JPEG upright according to its EXIF orientation

options.name: --strict
options.description: Fail with unsupported-feature instead of skipping a picture or shape the library cannot draw

options.name: --file-access
options.description: Which local files a document may reference: any (default; every regular file, like Pandoc), roots (only inside the --allow-root folders), no-symlinks (no symbolic link or junction), or roots,no-symlinks

options.name: --allow-root
options.description: A folder the referenced files may be in (repeatable; implies --file-access roots); without it roots allows the current folder and the folder of each input

options.name: --view
options.description: SCAD model: the viewpoint - iso (default; top for a model that is entirely 2D), front, back, left, right, top, or bottom

options.name: --azimuth
options.description: SCAD model: replace the azimuth of the view, in degrees about the Z axis (0 = from the front)

options.name: --elevation
options.description: SCAD model: replace the elevation of the view, in degrees above the XY plane (-90 to 90)

options.name: --projection
options.description: SCAD model: ortho (default) or perspective

options.name: --define
options.description: SCAD model: set a variable, for example -D width=20 or -D label=text (repeatable)

options.name: --time
options.description: SCAD model: the value of $t, the animation time (default 0)

options.name: --default-color
options.description: SCAD model: the color of surfaces the model does not color (default gray)

options.name: --max-triangles
options.description: SCAD model: the most triangles the model may produce (default 5000000)

options.name: --a-view
options.description: SCAD model: the viewpoint of the first input (overrides --view)

options.name: --b-view
options.description: SCAD model: the viewpoint of the second input (overrides --view)

options.name: --a-define
options.description: SCAD model: set a variable of the first input (repeatable; wins over -D of the same name)

options.name: --b-define
options.description: SCAD model: set a variable of the second input (repeatable; wins over -D of the same name)

options.name: --resize-to
options.description: Bring both inputs to one size: a (the size of the first input), b (the second), or WxH

options.name: --fit
options.description: How a raster input is fitted to --resize-to: contain (default; keeps the aspect ratio, with margins) or stretch

options.name: --filter
options.description: Resampling filter of a resize or fit: auto (default), nearest, bilinear, bicubic, lanczos3, or area

options.name: --tolerance
options.description: A pixel differs when a channel differs by more than this, 0-255 (default 8)

options.name: --grid
options.description: Report the error of each cell of a grid, columns x rows, each 1-64 (default 4x4)

options.name: --threshold
options.description: Fail (exit code 1) unless a metric is within a limit: mae, rmse, max-diff, diff-ratio, or cell-rmse at most; psnr or ssim at least (repeatable)

options.name: --diff
options.description: Write a picture of the differences to this file

options.name: --diff-style
options.description: How --diff draws a difference: heat (default) or abs; --side-by-side always uses heat

options.name: --gain
options.description: Amplification of a difference in the pictures, 0.1-255 (default 4)

options.name: --side-by-side
options.description: Write the first input, the second input, and the differences side by side to this file

options.name: --overlay
options.description: Write a blend of both inputs to this file

options.name: --overlay-weight
options.description: Weight of the second input in --overlay, 0-1 (default 0.5)

options.name: --quality
options.description: JPEG quality, 1-100 (default 90)

options.name: --no-clobber
options.description: Fail instead of overwriting an existing output file

options.name: --version
options.description: Display version information

options.name: --help
options.description: Display this help message

options.name: --silent
options.description: Suppress console output

options.name: --validate
options.description: Run self-validation

options.name: --json
options.description: Write the result as one JSON document to standard output

options.name: --results
options.description: Write validation results to file (.trx or .xml)

options.name: --depth
options.description: Set heading depth for markdown output (default: 1)

options.name: --log
options.description:
Write output to log file
See also: 'canvasnet help <topic>' for what a format supports, examples, and
known differences (topics: scad, vega-lite, mermaid, svg, pdf, pptx, vsdx,
raster, json, errors, limits, files), and 'canvasnet help topics' to list
them.
--diff, --side-by-side, and --overlay write pictures of the differences. --threshold makes the command fail
--page, --dpi, and the SCAD options apply to both inputs; --a-page, --b-page, --a-dpi, --b-dpi, --a-view,
--b-view, --a-define, and --b-define apply to one input and win. Either input may end in a fragment

commands.name: convert
commands.description: Render or convert an image, drawing, or document page to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or TIFF, with optional transformations

options.name: --page
options.description: The page or slide to render, counted from 1 (default 1)

options.name: --all-pages
options.description: Render every page or slide; the output must contain {page} or be a directory

options.name: --dpi
options.description: Resolution of a PDF, PPTX, or VSDX page in dots per inch (default 96; VSDX needs a whole number)

options.name: --scale
options.description: Multiply the natural size by a factor, for example 2 or 0.5

options.name: --width
options.description: Target width in pixels; the height keeps the aspect ratio unless --height is given

options.name: --height
options.description: Target height in pixels; the width keeps the aspect ratio unless --width is given

options.name: --size
options.description: Exact target size, for example 800x600 (shorthand for --width and --height)

options.name: --background
options.description: Color to flatten transparency over: white (default for vector sources), black, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, transparent

options.name: --no-auto-orient
options.description: Do not turn a JPEG upright according to its EXIF orientation

options.name: --strict
options.description: Fail with unsupported-feature instead of skipping a picture or shape the library cannot draw

options.name: --file-access
options.description: Which local files a document may reference: any (default; every regular file, like Pandoc), roots (only inside the --allow-root folders), no-symlinks (no symbolic link or junction), or roots,no-symlinks

options.name: --allow-root
options.description: A folder the referenced files may be in (repeatable; implies --file-access roots); without it roots allows the current folder and the folder of each input

options.description: SCAD model: the viewpoint - iso (default; top for a model that is entirely 2D), front, back, left, right, top, or bottom

options.name: --azimuth
options.description: SCAD model: replace the azimuth of the view, in degrees about the Z axis (0 = from the front)

options.name: --projection
options.description: SCAD model: ortho (default) or perspective

options.name: --define
options.description: SCAD model: set a variable, for example -D width=20 or -D label=text (repeatable)

options.name: --time
options.description: SCAD model: the value of $t, the animation time (default 0)

options.name: --default-color
options.description: SCAD model: the color of surfaces the model does not color (default gray)

options.name: --max-triangles
options.description: SCAD model: the most triangles the model may produce (default 5000000)

options.name: --param
options.description: Vega-Lite chart: set a parameter, for example --param cutoff=50 or --param brush={"x":[2,6]} (repeatable)

options.name: --theme
options.description: Mermaid diagram: the theme - default, base, dark, forest, or neutral (a theme the diagram sets itself wins)

options.name: --crop
options.description: Crop to a rectangle x,y,w,h or WxH+X+Y, each value in pixels or percent (repeatable; operations run in the order written)

options.name: --resize
options.description: Resample to exactly this size, for example 800x600

options.name: --fit
options.description: Shrink to fit inside this box, keeping the aspect ratio (an image that already fits is unchanged)

options.name: --allow-upscale
options.description: Let --fit enlarge an image that is smaller than the box

options.name: --rotate
options.description: Rotate clockwise by any angle in degrees, for example 90 or -3.5; an angle that is not a multiple of 90 grows the canvas and fills the corners (see --rotate-fill)

options.name: --rotate-fill
options.description: Color of the corners a --rotate or --deskew exposes (default: the --background, else white for an opaque image, else transparent)

options.name: --flip
options.description: Mirror: h (left to right), v (top to bottom), or both

options.name: --pad
options.description: Add a border of N pixels on every side, or l,t,r,b pixels on each side

options.name: --pad-color
options.description: Color of the border added by --pad (default: the --background, else white for a drawing or document, else transparent)

options.name: --grayscale
options.description: Turn every pixel gray (its luma); transparency is kept

options.name: --invert
options.description: Invert the colors; transparency is kept

options.name: --threshold
options.description: Turn the image black and white: pixels with a luma above the level (0-255) become white; auto chooses the level with Otsu's method

options.name: --levels
options.description: Map the levels black..white to 0..255, with an optional gamma (0.1-10; above 1 brightens the midtones), for example 20,230 or 20,230,1.2

options.name: --brightness
options.description: Add an amount (-255 to 255) to every color level

options.name: --contrast
options.description: Change the contrast around mid-gray by a percentage (-100 to 100)

options.name: --auto-levels
options.description: Stretch the levels so the darkest and lightest pixels become black and white (ignoring 1% of the pixels at each end; see --auto-levels-clip)

options.name: --auto-levels-clip
options.description: Percentage of the pixels --auto-levels ignores at each end, 0-20 (default 1)

options.name: --deskew
options.description: Straighten the image: find the tilt of its near-horizontal lines (within 15 degrees) and rotate it level; the angle is in the --json result

options.name: --trim
options.description: Crop away the uniform border around the content (the background is the most common color of the four corners)

options.name: --trim-tolerance
options.description: How far a pixel may differ from the background and still count as background, 0-255 (default 8)

options.name: --grid
options.description: Draw a labeled coordinate grid with a line every N pixels (8-4096) in the color given (default #FF00FFA0); put it last to read the final coordinates

options.name: --filter
options.description: Resampling filter of a resize or fit: auto (default), nearest, bilinear, bicubic, lanczos3, or area

options.name: --output
options.description: The output file; its extension selects the format

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: png, jpeg, bmp, or tiff (overrides the extension)

options.name: --quality
options.description: JPEG quality, 1-100 (default 90)

options.description: Fail instead of overwriting an existing output file

options.name: --file-access
options.description:
Chooses the mode for render and its verbs, inspect, compare, montage,
and flatten: any, roots, no-symlinks, or roots,no-symlinks, in any
letter case. Anything else is a usage-error that lists the modes. info
always measures under any.

options.name: --allow-root
options.description:
A folder that referenced files may be in; repeatable. It implies
--file-access roots and replaces the default folders. A relative folder
is taken from the current folder, and a folder that does not exist is a
usage-error. With --file-access any or no-symlinks it is a usage-error
that names the conflict.
In every mode:
inputs
The files named on the command line are never judged by the mode, only
the files they reference: images, pictures, data files, includes, and
linked pages, at every level.
never read
A network URL (http:, https:, and other schemes), a UNC or network path,
a file: URI with a host, a device path, an alternate data stream, and
anything that is not a regular file are never read.
limits
Every size and count limit holds in every mode; a mode decides which
files may be read, never how much. See 'canvasnet help limits'.
Diagnostics and errors:
image-access-denied
Warning: a picture (an SVG image, a Mermaid picture, a Vega-Lite image
mark, or a linked page) that the mode denies is not drawn, and the rest
is; the message names the link, the mode, and why. With --strict it is
the error file-access-denied.
file-access-denied
Error: an OpenSCAD include or use file or a Vega-Lite data file that the
mode denies, or a denied picture with --strict; the message names the
file as written and where it is referenced. No output is written.
real path unavailable
A mode other than any needs the real path of every opened file. Where
the system cannot tell it (Linux without /proc, for example), the file
is denied, never read unchecked.
detail
In the JSON result, the detail of an image-access-denied note holds the
reference, the requested and real paths, and the mode. These are host
paths: a service that shows notes to untrusted authors should remove
them.
The Pandoc filter:
default
docs/filters/canvasnet.lua passes no mode, so a document reads its
pictures, includes, and data as Pandoc reads its images.
CANVASNET_FILE_ACCESS
Set it to roots, no-symlinks, or roots,no-symlinks to pass --file-access
to every render and flatten of the filter; a picture the mode denies
then stops the build.
CANVASNET_ROOTS
Folders separated like PATH (; on Windows, : elsewhere), passed as one
--allow-root each as an absolute path (a relative folder is taken from
the working directory); it implies roots. Without it, roots gets the
working directory and the folder of the picture as --allow-root. These
arguments are part of the cache name of every picture, so a picture
drawn without them, or from another working directory, is not reused.

commands.name: json
commands.description:
With --json every command writes exactly one JSON document, on
one line, to standard output.

commands.name: anchors
commands.description:
Only for an OpenSCAD model: the points it declared with echo("anchor",
"name", [x, y, z]), in echo order, each {name, point: [x, y, z], pixel:
[x, y] or null, inside}. pixel is the position in the written picture,
from its top-left corner, after the pixel steps; see 'canvasnet help
scad'.

commands.name: code
commands.description:
The stable generic identifier of the report, for example
scad-module-surface, vl-mark-geoshape, svg-image-unresolved, or
image-page-out-of-range. A warning of a SCAD model always has the code
scad-warning, a warning of a Vega-Lite chart the code vega-lite-warning,
and a warning of a Mermaid diagram the code mermaid-warning; the finer
identifier is in detail.

commands.name: compare
commands.description:
Described in their own help: run 'canvasnet help compare', 'canvasnet
help montage', or 'canvasnet help inspect'.

commands.name: detail
commands.description:
Only when the code is generic: the finer identifier of the library, for
example scad-anchor-invalid for a scad-warning, vl-unknown-property for
a vega-lite-warning, or mermaid-config-unknown-key for a
mermaid-warning. Branch on code and detail, never on the message.

commands.name: diagnostics
commands.description:
The features that were left out of the picture; see the diagnostics
section below.

commands.name: diagram
commands.description:
For a Mermaid diagram (info): {type, supported, direction, title,
accTitle, nodes, edges, subgraphs}. type is the diagram type (flowchart
for flowchart and graph, sequence for sequenceDiagram); supported is
false for a type this version does not draw (journey, timeline, and so
on), which renders as an empty picture with the diagnostic
mermaid-diagram-unsupported; nodes, edges, and subgraphs count the
participants, the messages, and the boxes of a sequence diagram, the
classes, relations, and namespaces of a class diagram, the states,
transitions, and composite states of a state diagram, and the entities,
relationships, and subgraphs of an entity relationship diagram; nodes
counts the slices of a pie chart (its legend entries) and the tasks of a
gantt chart (its vertical markers included), subgraphs the sections of a
gantt chart, and edges is 0 for both; nodes and edges count the nodes of
a mindmap and the edges between them (one fewer than the nodes), and
subgraphs is 0; nodes counts the blocks of a packet diagram as written,
and edges and subgraphs are 0; nodes and edges count the commits of a
git graph and the links from each commit to its parents, subgraphs is 0,
and direction is LR, TB, or BT; direction, title, and accTitle are
present when the diagram has them.

commands.name: echo
commands.description: The text an OpenSCAD model printed with echo.

commands.name: error
commands.description:
{code, message, hint}: code is one of the stable codes of the errors
topic ('canvasnet help errors'); hint is omitted when there is none. The
document has no exit-code field: the exit code of every failure is 1.
- A failure document is written only when --json is given and --silent is
not. A failed compare gate also carries the fields of the comparison.

commands.name: flatten
commands.description:
tool, input {path, format, natural}, scale, flattened (false when
nothing was replaced and nothing was written), replaced[] ({href,
format, width, height, elements, bytes}: each link that became a PNG
picture, with the number of image elements that use it and the size of
the PNG), rebased[] ({href, newHref}: the relative links rewritten for
the folder of the copy), outputs[] ({path, format, bytes}; empty when
nothing was written), diagnostics, and echo.

commands.name: formats
commands.description:
tool, library, inputs[], outputs[], quality {min, max, default}, and
maxDimension. Each inputs[] entry has format, kind, extensions,
multiPage, vector, and helpTopic: the topic of 'canvasnet help <topic>'
that describes the format (raster for png, jpeg, bmp, tiff, gif, and
jpeg2000).

commands.name: help
commands.description:
kind is index, command, topic, examples, or example; see the help
section below.

commands.name: info
commands.description:
input {path, format, bytes} and one of image, document {pageCount,
pages[]}, model {modules, functions, directives}, chart, or diagram
(chart and diagram follow an image object with the laid-out size).

commands.name: input
commands.description:
{path, format, natural: {width, height}}, and for a document pageCount
and page; and fragment, the text after the # of an input path such as
part.scad#def.width=20 (path is then the file; the member is absent for
an input without a fragment). The same member is in the a and b of
compare and in each cell of montage.

commands.name: location
commands.description:
Only when the file gave a position: {file, line, column} for a model or
a diagram, or {file, pointer, line, column} for a chart (the JSON
pointer of the offending property); a member that is not known is left
out.

commands.name: message
commands.description:
A description; for a model, chart, or diagram it gives file, line, and
column.

commands.name: operations
commands.description:
Every step that was applied, in order; each has an op key (render,
embed, auto-orient, resize, fit, flatten, crop, rotate, flip, pad, and
the photo operations) and its own fields. With --all-pages every
operation also carries its page. The verbs are crop, resize, rotate,
flip, and pad.

commands.name: origin
commands.description:
Only for a report about an embedded file (an SVG that links other
files): the files, outermost first, that lead to it, as folder-relative
names (a link that was not drawn names the SVG file that contains it).
The message starts with the href as written.

commands.name: outputs
commands.description:
One entry per file written: {path, format, width, height, bytes} and
page for a document.

commands.name: page
commands.description:
The page of a document the report belongs to.
- Without --json the same reports are written to standard error as
'Unsupported: <code>: <message>' or 'Warning: <code>: <message>' lines
(and echo as 'ECHO: <text>'); with --json standard error carries none of
them, so standard output stays one JSON document.

commands.name: severity
commands.description:
unsupported for a feature that was left out, or warning for a
questionable construct that still rendered.

commands.name: source
commands.description:
Where the report comes from: scad, vega-lite, mermaid, pptx, vsdx, or
svg. PDF and raster images have no diagnostics channel.

commands.name: tool
commands.description: {name, version} of the tool.

commands.name: limits
commands.description:
The largest sizes and budgets the tool accepts, and the error
each one produces.

options.name: --dpi
options.description:
Above 0 and at most 2400 (PDF, PPTX, VSDX; a VSDX needs a whole number).
The default is 96. A page is its size in points times the dpi divided by
72.

options.name: --quality
options.description: JPEG quality 1 to 100, default 90.

commands.name: mermaid
commands.description:
A Mermaid flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, state
diagram, entity relationship diagram, pie chart, gantt chart,
mindmap, packet diagram, or git graph is laid out like Mermaid 11
and drawn as one still picture with the bundled fonts.

options.name: --theme
options.description:
The theme: default, base, dark, forest, or neutral, like mmdc -t. A
theme the diagram sets in its frontmatter or a directive still wins. In
a link or an input path the fragment theme=dark does the same
(flow.mmd#theme=dark). On any other kind of input --theme is a
usage-error.

options.name: --scale
options.description:
The natural size is Mermaid's SVG view box in pixels; --scale, --width,
and --height draw the diagram sharply at another size (a diagram larger
than 8192 pixels on a side needs one of them).

options.name: --background
options.description:
The color under the diagram: white by default, transparent keeps the
transparency of Mermaid's own SVG.

options.name: --strict
options.description:
Every unsupported construct, and a picture that is not drawn, becomes an
unsupported-feature error.
Diagnostics and errors:
mermaid-warning
The code of every warning of a diagram; the specific mermaid-* code is
in detail and the line and column in location.
mermaid-shape-unknown
Error (mermaid-error): a shape name Mermaid does not define; the hint
names the nearest one.
mermaid-syntax-error
Error (mermaid-error): the text does not follow the grammar of its
diagram type; the message gives the line, the column, and the tokens
that were expected, and the hint suggests the fix.
mermaid-unknown-diagram
Error (mermaid-error): the first statement is not a Mermaid diagram
keyword; the hint names the nearest one.
mermaid-yaml-invalid
Error (mermaid-error): the frontmatter or the shape data is not valid
YAML; anchors, aliases, and tags are refused (mermaid-yaml-unsupported).
mermaid-limit-exceeded
Error (budget-exceeded): a limit of the library (nodes, edges, nesting,
label length, layout work, pictures, painted pixels); see 'canvasnet
help limits'.
mermaid-render-failed
Error (mermaid-error): the diagram cannot be laid out, for example a
subgraph that contains itself, an empty sequence block, two composite
states that contain each other, or a gantt task whose date is invalid or
whose after and until references go in a circle.
mermaid-participant-type-unknown
Warning: a sequence participant has a type Mermaid does not define; it
is not drawn, as in Mermaid, and the hint names the nearest type.
mermaid-config-unknown-key
Warning: a configuration key Mermaid does not define; it is ignored.
mermaid-config-invalid
Warning: a configuration value of the wrong type or range, or a theme
that is not available; it is ignored (sequence.textPlacement: fo is
drawn with the default placement).
mermaid-config-secure-key
Warning: the text tried to change a secure key (securityLevel,
maxTextSize, maxEdges, and so on); the change is ignored.
mermaid-style-ignored
Warning: a style declaration outside the supported subset; it is
ignored.
mermaid-html-tag-ignored
Warning: an HTML tag outside the supported label subset; the tag is
dropped and its text is kept.
mermaid-image-unresolved
Warning: a picture the resolver did not give; the node keeps its frame.
- A link that is not drawn (a missing file, a network URL) is the warning
svg-image-unresolved with the reason, a link the file-access mode denies
is image-access-denied, and --strict makes either a failure.
mermaid-text-missing-glyph
Warning: a character that no bundled font has (for example CJK); it is
drawn as the missing-glyph box.
mermaid-gantt-today-unavailable
Warning: a gantt chart needs today (a todayMarker style, an after or
until id that no task has, or a date without a year, month, or day) and
MermaidRenderOptions.Now is not set; the today line is not drawn and
1970-01-01 is taken as today.
mermaid-gantt-ticks-skipped
Warning: the tickInterval of a gantt chart spans more than 10,000 of its
intervals (Mermaid's estimate of the ticks; exactly 10,000 draws 10,001
ticks, both ends included); the default ticks are drawn, as in Mermaid.
mermaid-gantt-excludes-skipped
Warning: the tasks of a gantt chart with excluded days span more than
five years; the excluded days are not shaded, as in Mermaid.
mermaid-diagnostics-suppressed
Warning: more reports than MaxDiagnostics; the rest are dropped.
- A text longer than 50000 characters is corrupt-input.
Known differences from Mermaid:
- Text is measured and drawn with the bundled Liberation Sans (Mermaid's
default trebuchet ms, verdana, and arial map to it) and the bundled Noto
fallback fonts, never an installed font, so the result does not depend on
the machine; against Mermaid rendered with the same font the layout
matches to a hundredth of a pixel.
- The circles of the new shapes are true circles where Mermaid draws
rough.js curves (a few hundredths of a pixel).
- The picture is static: no interaction, and an animated edge is drawn as
its first frame.
- info lays the diagram out without the pictures of its nodes (it reads no
other file), so a picture node without w and h can make the drawn diagram
a little larger or smaller than the size info reports (with --width or
--height it is fitted into the box); give an @{ img } node its w and h
(constraint on) so that the layout does not depend on the picture. A
render without --width and --height reports the natural size of the
diagram it drew (the natural size of render --json); a library render of
the diagram file without a size (CanvasNetViewer.Render) also charges its
pixel budget for that drawn size, while a document that embeds the diagram
always gives it a size.
- A diagram is drawn over white unless --background says otherwise
(Mermaid's SVG is transparent); as a picture in an SVG file it stays
transparent.
- Mermaid crashes on some invalid graphs (a subgraph cycle, a link to a
subgraph without an anchor, two composite states that contain each other,
a note on a state that appears nowhere before it, a relationship to an
entity named like a subgraph declared after it, a relationship from a
subgraph to an entity inside it); these are a located mermaid-error
instead.
- Interaction (click, href, call, tooltips, the link and callback of a class
diagram, and the click of a state diagram or a gantt chart) is read and
ignored without a report, because a picture is static.
- Mermaid draws a broken sequence diagram or fails for an empty block (a
block with no message or note inside), for link or links on an actor,
boundary, control, or entity participant, and for a properties icon that
is not text; these are a located mermaid-render-failed instead.
- $$ math is drawn and measured as written (mermaid-math-unsupported), and
textPlacement: fo (HTML labels) is drawn with the default placement.
- The color keywords and system colors of a box or a rect background take
the values of headless Chrome in the light scheme (system colors depend on
the platform in a browser).
- The width of a text is the advance of its glyphs grown to the pixels its
first and last glyphs reach, as Chrome measures it; for fonts or sizes
other than those of the reference diagrams, a width can differ by a pixel,
which can move the margins by up to a pixel.
- With htmlLabels: false the texts of a class box are SVG text, measured as
Chrome measures them; Chrome's box of a few glyphs at the end of a text is
a pixel wider, so such a class box can differ from Mermaid's by up to a
pixel.
- Mermaid's fix-up of an SVG class text that holds &gt (a generic) is not
ported; the entities are decoded instead, which gives the same characters
for a text of one line.
- $$ math in a class text is drawn and measured as written, without a
report.
- A style declaration of a class, state, or entity relationship diagram
outside the supported subset is reported at the first mention of the
class, state, or entity, not at the style statement.
- A corner radius (rx or ry) in a style, a classDef, or themeCSS is ignored
with a mermaid-style-ignored warning; the radii of Mermaid's own style
sheet are drawn.
- The texts of class and state diagrams are always cleaned as at Mermaid's
strict level; securityLevel changes nothing.
- Mermaid's legacy state renderer is not ported: a stateDiagram with another
state.defaultRenderer is drawn with the current renderer and reported as
mermaid-layout-unsupported at the state key of the configuration.
- The direction info reports for a state or entity relationship diagram is
the last top-level direction statement, the one the diagram is laid out
in, where Mermaid's getDirection gives the first.
- The last concurrent region of a composite state has the id id-random-N
where Mermaid's id holds a random number; the id is never drawn.
- Mermaid's entity relationship markers clip the line at the edge of their
view port, which hides half of the stroke at the tip; the clip is not
modeled, so a tip can be half a stroke longer.
- With htmlLabels: false the texts of an entity table take the style sheet's
label color (nodeTextColor, else textColor), where Chrome uses textColor;
the two are the same in the built-in themes.
- The marker shapes of the neo look and the entity colors of the redux
themes are not drawn (the look is reported, and the themes are not
available).
- The today of a gantt chart is the time the caller gives
(MermaidRenderOptions.Now), never the clock; the tool, the Viewer, and the
Pandoc filter give none, so the today line is not drawn and 1970-01-01 is
taken as today (mermaid-gantt-today-unavailable where it matters). Write
todayMarker off, or give the dates in full, to keep the warning away.
- The dates of a gantt chart are in UTC, where Mermaid uses the time zone of
the browser, so a chart never changes with the machine or with daylight
saving time.
- A gantt start date that matches neither the dateFormat nor an ISO form
(2024-1-5, Jan 5 2024, which browsers read in their own ways) is a located
mermaid-render-failed Invalid date.
- Mermaid fails, or draws a broken chart, for the topAxis statement, a task
whose data holds only tags, a first task without a start, a task with more
than three fields, after or until references that go in a circle, excluded
days that never end, a compact section named like a JavaScript object
member (constructor, toString), and a dateFormat with the week (w, ww, wo,
gggg) or zone name (z, zzz) tokens; these are a located
mermaid-syntax-error or mermaid-render-failed instead.
- A gantt chart is 784 pixels wide, the width Mermaid takes in the page of
mmdc, unless gantt.useWidth is set (in a browser it takes the width of the
page), and its ticks keep d3's half-pixel offset at every scale.
- The opacity of a pie slice, a gantt section row, and the gantt grid is
folded into its colors, so where two of them overlap the colors can differ
slightly; the turn of a milestone and the enlargement of a highlighted
slice are applied to the outline, and the crisp edges of the gantt grid
are drawn antialiased.
- A character that no bundled font has is drawn as the missing-glyph box in
a pie, gantt, packet, or git graph text without the warning
mermaid-text-missing-glyph.
- The links of a gantt chart (click ... href) are always checked as at
Mermaid's strict level and kept only as data.
- A mindmap is laid out exactly as Mermaid's cose-bilkent lays it out when
its node sizes are Mermaid's, up to 1,016 nodes (above that, a few node
counts differ where Chrome's pow is not correctly rounded). The layout is
chaotic: a node whose size differs slightly from Chrome's (such as a cloud
or a bang, whose arcs Chrome measures in single precision) can move other
nodes far. The layout is the same on every machine.
- The icons of a mindmap (::icon(...)) are not drawn, as in Mermaid 11, and
are reported (mermaid-icon-unsupported).
- Another mindmap layout (dagre, elk, tidy-tree, and others that mmdc can
load) is reported (mermaid-layout-unsupported), and the mindmap is laid
out with cose-bilkent.
- A mindmap of the keyword alone has no view box in Mermaid; here it is an
empty picture of the margin, 20 by 20 pixels at the default padding.
- An ::icon(...) or a ::: class before the first node of a mindmap, which
Mermaid fails on with a script error, is a located mermaid-syntax-error.
- The depth of a mindmap is bounded by MaxNestingDepth, where Mermaid has no
limit, and a mindmap of about 1,000 nodes or more can reach the layout
work limit (MaxLayoutWork).
- MaxNodes bounds the blocks of a packet diagram and the parts that its rows
split them into, so a range that Mermaid splits into thousands of rows
(such as 0-99999999) fails with mermaid-limit-exceeded at the default
limits; with a raised limit, Mermaid's own cap of 10,000 rows is kept.
- A packet setting of the wrong type is mermaid-config-invalid and ignored,
where Mermaid computes with it. A fractional, zero, or negative
packet.bitsPerRow splits the blocks exactly as Mermaid splits them, and
where Mermaid then fails with Block start ... is greater than block end
..., the render is a located mermaid-render-failed. Every block is checked
when the text is read, so an invalid block is always the
mermaid-syntax-error, where Mermaid can fail at an earlier split first.
- A commit without an id is given an id of the same form as Mermaid's (its
number, a dash, and seven hexadecimal digits, such as 0-eb28011), but the
digits come from a fixed pseudo-random sequence that starts again for
every diagram, where Mermaid draws random digits in every render, so the
picture is the same every time.
- MaxNodes counts the main branch, the branches, and the commits of a git
graph; MaxLabelLength also bounds the messages and tags that Mermaid
composes for merges and cherry-picks, so a long chain of cherry-picks of
cherry-picks fails with mermaid-limit-exceeded; a git graph of more than
about 650 commits in one direction needs --scale, --width, or --height to
fit the largest picture.
- A git graph setting of the wrong type is mermaid-config-invalid and
ignored. A site configuration that renames or reorders the main branch
runs the statements again when the git graph is drawn, where an operation
that then fails is a located mermaid-render-failed; where Mermaid's git
graph renderer fails (Closest parent not found for commit ...), the render
is a located mermaid-render-failed.
- The width of a commit id or tag of a git graph can be up to a pixel
narrower than Chrome's for a few glyphs at a few sizes (such as a 10-pixel
id that ends in D); a commit id used again replaces the earlier commit
without a report, as in Mermaid, which only logs a warning.

commands.name: pdf
commands.description:
Multi-page documents; a page is drawn as an image. There is no
diagnostics channel.

options.name: --page
options.description:
The page to draw, counted from 1 (default 1); a page beyond the last is
page-out-of-range.

options.name: --all-pages
options.description:
Draw every page; for a document of more than one page the output must
contain {page} or be a directory.

options.description:
Resolution in dots per inch (default 96, above 0 and at most 2400). A 72
by 48 point page is 96 by 64 pixels at 96 dpi.

options.name: --scale
options.description:
Multiply the natural size by a factor; --width, --height, and --size
also size the page.

options.name: --background
options.description: The color the page is flattened over (white by default).

options.name: --strict
options.description:
Accepted, but PDF has no diagnostics channel, so it changes nothing.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- None: the diagnostics[] list of a PDF is always empty and --strict has no
effect. A feature the renderer cannot draw is an error instead.
unsupported-feature
Error code: the message names the feature, for example
pdf-image-lab-decode or pdf-image-tint-budget.
corrupt-input
Error code: a damaged or truncated document.
page-out-of-range
Error code: --page is beyond the last page.
Known differences from PDF viewers:
- ICC profiles are not applied, so colors in ICCBased spaces can differ
slightly from a viewer.
- A substituted font is chosen from the installed fonts, so text with fonts
that are not embedded can differ between machines.
- Mesh shadings in DeviceCMYK, Separation, and DeviceN spaces are
approximated: each vertex is converted to RGB first and the result is
blended.
- Images are resampled once, so thin one pixel rules are attenuated rather
than dropped.

skipped. It is the only skipped-picture report; with --strict it is an

between machines.

commands.name: scad
commands.description:
A model is evaluated and drawn as one still picture from a named
viewpoint.

options.name: --view
options.description:
The viewpoint: iso (default; a model that is entirely 2D defaults to
top), front, back, left, right, top, or bottom.

options.name: --azimuth
options.description:
Replace the azimuth of the view: degrees about the Z axis, 0 from the
front.

options.name: --elevation
options.description:
Replace the elevation of the view: degrees above the XY plane, -90 to
90.

options.name: --projection
options.description: ortho (default) or perspective.

options.name: --define
options.description:
Set a variable of the model; -D is the short form. Repeatable; the later
definition wins. The value is a number, true, false, text, or a JSON
array for a vector. A def.<name>=<value> in the fragment of the input
(part.scad#def.width=20) wins over it for that input.

options.name: --time
options.description: The value of $t (default 0).

options.name: --default-color
options.description:
The color of surfaces the model does not color (default gray); the alpha
is ignored. A flat 2D drawing is gray by default, so --default-color
black gives a high-contrast drawing; a color() in the model overrides
it.

options.name: --max-triangles
options.description: The most triangles the model may produce (default 5000000).

options.name: --size
options.description:
The picture is 800x800 pixels unless a size option is given; --width,
--height, and --scale also size it. The camera fits the picture; nothing
is stretched.

options.name: --background
options.description:
The color the picture is flattened over (default white; black, #RRGGBB,
or #RRGGBBAA); transparent keeps alpha.

options.name: --strict
options.description:
Fail with unsupported-feature instead of leaving a construct out.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- Without --strict an unsupported construct is left out and listed in
diagnostics[] of the JSON result as {source: scad, severity: unsupported,
code: <id>} (without --json, as an 'Unsupported: <id>: <message>' line on
standard error). With --strict the first one fails with
unsupported-feature and no file is written.
- The output of echo() is in echo[] of the JSON result as 'ECHO: <text>'
lines; without --json it is written to standard error in the same form.
scad-module-offset
Also scad-module-surface, scad-module-import, and scad-module-roof: the
module and its children are omitted.
scad-projection-too-complex
A projection needs more work than one projection may do (too many
triangles, or a difference or an intersection whose silhouette costs too
much to classify): the projection is omitted.
scad-projection-open-mesh
A projection found a mesh that is not a closed solid (its cross-section
does not close): the projection is omitted.
scad-hull-csg-operand
A hull has a difference or an intersection among its children.
scad-hull-mixed-dimensions
A hull has both 2D and 3D children.
scad-minkowski-nonconvex
A minkowski has a child that is not convex.
scad-minkowski-2d
A minkowski of 2D children.
scad-minkowski-mixed-dimensions
A minkowski has both 2D and 3D children.
scad-modifier-highlight
# on a 2D shape that is not extruded: drawn normally, without highlight.
scad-modifier-background
% on a 2D shape that is not extruded: omitted.
scad-multmatrix-projective
multmatrix with a bottom row other than [0, 0, 0, 1]: omitted.
scad-resize-approximate
resize over children that contain a difference or an intersection:
estimated bounds are used.
scad-function-<name>
An unimplemented built-in function, for example
scad-function-textmetrics: the call evaluates to undef.
scad-warning
Severity warning: a questionable argument (an invalid argument, for
example) that still renders.
scad-error
Error code: a syntax error, an evaluation error, or an include that
cannot be read; the message names file, line, and column.
budget-exceeded
Error code: the model needs more triangles than --max-triangles allows.
- See the OpenSCAD section of the Scad user guide for the complete list of
identifiers.
Anchors (callout points):
- echo("anchor", "name", [x, y, z]); declares a named point of the model,
for a callout or a leader line drawn on the picture later. The echo line
is still printed. The point is in the coordinate system where the
statement stands: every enclosing translate, rotate, scale, mirror, and
multmatrix is applied, so the anchor is a world point. Only the statement
form counts; an echo used as an expression, or inside a function, is a
plain echo.
- A module, for, if, union, difference, intersection, render, color, hull,
or minkowski does not move its children, so the point passes through
unchanged. An anchor inside resize, linear_extrude, rotate_extrude,
projection, or another module that cannot give its children a position is
skipped with a scad-anchor-invalid warning.
scad-anchor-invalid
Severity warning (code scad-warning, the identifier starts the message):
a malformed declaration (a name that is not a non-empty string, a point
that is not three finite numbers, a named or an extra argument) or an
anchor in an unsupported context. The anchor is skipped; the echo line
stays.
- The same name may be declared more than once; every declaration is kept,
in echo order.
- With --json, render adds anchors[] for a model: {name, point: [x, y, z],
pixel: [x, y], inside}. pixel is the position in the written picture in
pixels from its top-left corner (continuous: pixel i spans [i, i+1), so
the center of the first pixel is 0.5), projected with the camera that drew
the picture, perspective included. inside is true when pixel lies within
the picture. Without --json nothing is added.
- The pixel steps move the anchors with the picture: --crop, --trim,
--resize, --fit, --pad, --flip, and --rotate are applied to pixel, and
inside is tested against the final picture. After a --deskew that corrects
the image, pixel is null; it is also null for a point behind a perspective
camera (inside is then false).
- pixel says where a point projects, not whether it can be seen: an anchor
hidden behind other geometry still has a pixel and inside true.
Known differences from OpenSCAD:
- This is an independent dialect, not OpenSCAD: pictures and tessellation
are not pixel-identical to OpenSCAD and no parity is claimed.
- include and use are read relative to the folder of the file that names
them (any local file, as in OpenSCAD, unless --file-access says otherwise;
see 'canvasnet help files'), a missing include is an error here, and an
include the mode denies is the error file-access-denied.
- A model can be drawn inside an SVG diagram with <image href="part.scad"
.../> (see 'canvasnet help svg'), with the view the library chooses for it
(isometric for a 3D model, top-down for a flat 2D model, or the model's
own $vp* variables) over a transparent background. <image
href="part.scad#view=front" .../> chooses a named view instead (iso,
front, back, left, right, top, bottom); #view without a value, or an
unknown name, is image-fragment-invalid and the image is not drawn. Every
def.<name>=<value> in the fragment sets a variable of the model exactly
like -D name=value (same value grammar and precedence; a name that is not
an identifier, or a value that is not valid, is image-fragment-invalid),
for example <image href="part.scad#view=front&def.width=20" .../>; the
prefix def. means a variable can never collide with view. An input path of
the command line takes the same fragment (canvasnet render
"part.scad#view=front&def.width=20" -o part.png).
- Indexing is lenient: v[i] is undef for a negative or non-finite index, and
a fractional index is truncated.
- text() is laid out one character at a time without shaping or ligatures;
language and script are ignored; size is the height of the glyph H. A
generic name (sans, serif, mono, sans-serif, monospace, ...) is a bundled
Liberation font; any other family is looked up in the installed fonts (so
it can differ between machines), then among the bundled Liberation
families, and a family found nowhere is drawn with the bundled Liberation
Sans and a warning. For each character the chosen font lacks, the glyph
comes from the bundled Noto Sans, Noto Sans Math, or Noto Sans Symbols 2
(never an installed font), with no kerning across fonts; characters
nothing covers are listed in one warning per text().
- The semantics of the # highlight and the % ghost are this package's
documented choices; a ghost is part of the fitted bounds but not of the
model.
- hull and minkowski constructs they cannot handle are omitted and reported,
never approximated; so is a projection that is too complex or whose mesh
is not closed.
- projection(cut = true) includes a face that lies exactly in the z = 0
plane (a closed section); the silhouette and the section are computed from
the tessellated meshes, so a curved solid projects to its polygon.
- The viewport variables follow the documented meaning of the OpenSCAD ones
($vpr is the rotation of the camera, so rotate($vpr) turns an object to
face it). The model sees the default $vpt = [0, 0, 0], $vpd = 140, and
$vpf = 22.5 and the $vpr of the requested view, because the camera is
fitted after the model is built; only an assignment of $vpt, $vpd, or $vpf
turns off the automatic framing.
- The result is a static picture from a named view (iso by default, top for
a model that is entirely 2D; orthographic by default), not an interactive
camera.

commands.name: svg
commands.description:
A common subset of SVG, drawn sharply at the target size. An
image can embed a picture, another SVG file, a model, a chart, a
Mermaid diagram, or a document page, named relative to the SVG
file.

options.name: --width
options.description:
Draw at this width, keeping the aspect ratio; --height does the same for
the height. The drawing is sharp, never enlarged afterwards.

options.name: --size
options.description: Draw inside this box, centered and never stretched.

options.name: --scale
options.description: Multiply the intrinsic size by a factor.

options.name: --background
options.description:
The color transparency is flattened over (white by default); transparent
keeps alpha.

options.name: --file-access
options.description:
Which local files the image elements may read: any (the default), roots,
no-symlinks, or roots,no-symlinks; --allow-root names the folders of
roots. See 'canvasnet help files'.

options.name: --strict
options.description:
An image that was not drawn (svg-image-unresolved, svg-image-too-large,
image-fragment-invalid, or image-page-out-of-range) is an
unsupported-feature error instead of a warning, image-access-denied is
the error file-access-denied, and an unsupported feature of an embedded
model, chart, or diagram is an unsupported-feature error too. The
warnings image-fragment-unknown-parameter,
image-fragment-duplicate-parameter, and vl-param-unknown stay warnings:
the picture was drawn.
Diagnostics and --strict:
svg-image-unresolved
Warning: an image href was not drawn. The message names the href and
why: not found, a network URL, a format the tool cannot draw, a cycle,
or a limit. With --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.
svg-image-too-large
Warning: an image was not drawn because its picture does not fit in the
pixel budget of the render. The message names the href and the pixels it
needs. With --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.
image-access-denied
Warning: an image href names a local file that the file-access mode
(--file-access, --allow-root) denies, so it was not read. The message
names the href, the mode, and why. --strict makes it the error
file-access-denied.
image-fragment-unknown-parameter
Warning: the fragment of an href names a parameter the linked file does
not use (a typo such as pag=2, or any parameter on a raster or an SVG
file). The picture is drawn without it. --strict does not fail on it.
image-fragment-duplicate-parameter
Warning: the fragment gives a parameter twice with different values; the
last one is used. --strict does not fail on it.
vl-param-unknown
Warning: a param.<name> of the fragment names a param the chart does not
declare (a typo, or a chart without params). The chart is drawn without
it. --strict does not fail on it.
image-fragment-invalid
Unsupported: a value that is not allowed (page=0, page=abc, page=2.5, an
empty value, an unknown view name, a def. value that is not valid JSON
when it starts with [ or a name that is not an identifier, a param.
value that is not valid JSON) or a fragment over its limit. The image is
not drawn; with --strict it is an unsupported-feature error. For an
input path of the command line the same mistake is an error with this
code.
image-page-out-of-range
Unsupported: the page or slide does not exist (page=9 of a 2-page
document). The image is not drawn and the message tells how many pages
there are; with --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.
svg-flatten-image-not-drawn
Warning of canvasnet flatten: an image links a file only CanvasNet
draws, but the drawing, or an SVG file it shows, never shows it (hidden,
an unused definition, outside the canvas, or over a limit of the
drawing), so it was left as a link. The location gives its file, line
and column; for a link of a nested SVG file the origin lists the files
that contain it. --strict does not fail on it.
- With --json each of these reports carries the embedding file in origin
(see 'canvasnet help json'); the message starts with the href as written.
- The notes of an embedded model, chart, diagram, or SVG file are reported
too, each starting with the href of the file, and the lines an embedded
model prints with echo are kept.
- An embedded file that is found but is broken (a corrupt picture, a model
with a syntax error, a chart with a bad specification, a diagram with a
syntax error) is an error with its own code, and the message names both
files.
corrupt-input
Error code: malformed XML, a root element that is not svg, or a document
over a limit.
Known differences from browsers:
- No scripting, animation, or network resources; images are read relative to
the folder of the SVG file (any local file, as in Pandoc, unless
--file-access says otherwise), and only by the command line tool (the
library opts in with SvgLoadOptions.ImageResolver).
- Text is best effort without shaping. An installed family is used, so text
can differ between machines; generic and unknown families use the bundled
Liberation fonts. A character those lack (such as U+221D) is taken from
the bundled Noto fonts; a character nothing covers draws the font's
missing-glyph box with no diagnostic, because SVG rendering reports
nothing.
- Lengths: ex is the height of the font's x glyph and ch the advance of 0
(half an em when the font has no such glyph); a normal line height is 1.2
em; vw, vh, vmin, and vmax are percentages of the root viewport in user
units (the viewBox, else the root width and height), which differs from a
browser only when the two disagree; and percent in a gradient, pattern, or
mask coordinate is a fraction of 1 under objectBoundingBox (the default)
but is relative to the viewport (width for x, height for y, the diagonal
for r) under userSpaceOnUse, the same for a plain percent and one inside
calc(). An omitted gradient attribute with a percent default uses the same
basis: under userSpaceOnUse an omitted x2 is 100% of the viewport width
and an omitted cx, cy, and r are 50% of the viewport width, height, and
diagonal (fx and fy follow cx and cy), and a pattern without width or
height paints nothing. An omitted mask x, y, width, or height is -10%,
-10%, 120%, or 120% in both modes: of the shape's box under
objectBoundingBox, and of the viewport width or height under
userSpaceOnUse. lh and rlh follow the line-height of a style attribute,
style element, or font shorthand; inside line-height itself lh is the
parent's line height and rlh on the root is the initial 1.2 times 16, so a
line height never refers to itself. The root width and height can use
font-relative units (against the root's own font-size and line-height from
its attributes or style, so lh and rlh there use the root's own line
height), but a percent or viewport unit there is ignored. The keyword
sizes follow the browsers' table, not the CSS Fonts factors (9.6, 12,
14.2, 16, 19.2, 24, 32, and 48).
- A length that is not valid (an unknown unit, a space between number and
unit, a bad calc(), a calc() that resolves to a plain number) in a shape,
a text position, the stroke width, a dash pattern (stroke-dasharray), or a
dash offset (stroke-dashoffset) is corrupt-input. In a gradient, pattern,
or mask coordinate, or in the root width and height, it is ignored and the
default is used; an invalid font-size, line-height, or font shorthand is
dropped, so the next lower source applies, else the size is inherited (a
browser does the same).
- Units are not converted for: letter-spacing, word-spacing, tspan
positioning (x, y, dx, and dy on a tspan), the lists of dx and dy beyond
the first value on a text element, textLength, baseline-shift, and nested
svg elements (which are not drawn, so their width, height, x, and y are
never read).
- The drawing is rendered sharply at the target size, not rasterized first
and scaled afterwards.

commands.name: vega-lite
commands.description:
A chart is laid out and drawn as one still picture; a defined
subset of Vega-Lite 5 and 6.

options.name: --scale
options.description: Multiply the laid-out size by a factor.

options.name: --width
options.description:
Fit the chart to a width, keeping its aspect ratio; --height does the
same for the height.

options.name: --size
options.description: Fit the chart inside a box and center it.

options.name: --background
options.description:
Replace the background the chart declares (white when it declares none);
transparent keeps alpha.

options.name: --strict
options.description: Fail with unsupported-feature instead of leaving a construct out.

options.name: --page
options.description:
A chart has one page, so only 1 is valid; a larger number is
page-out-of-range.

options.name: --param
options.description:
Replace the default value of a param of the specification (repeatable;
the later one of a name wins). The value is true, false, null, a number,
text (region=EU), or a JSON array or object, so a selection takes its
initial state as in the specification: --param cutoff=50, --param
brush={"x":[2,6]} (quote it for your shell). A name the specification
does not declare is a vega-lite-error that lists the declared ones. The
chart is laid out again with the values, so its size can change; only a
chart takes it (a usage-error for any other input). An SVG file sets the
params of a chart it embeds with the fragment of the link: <image
href="chart.vl.json#param.cutoff=50" .../> (see 'canvasnet help svg'),
and so does an input path of the command line: canvasnet render
"chart.vl.json#param.cutoff=50" -o c.png (the fragment wins over --param
for that input; a name the chart does not declare is then the warning
vl-param-unknown instead of an error).
- The model options (-D, --view, ...) are a usage-error for a chart: -D is
for the variables of a model and --param for the params of a chart.
'canvasnet info' reports the laid-out size, marks, and data references
without drawing.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- Identifiers have the form vl-<area>-<detail>, in lower case. An
unsupported construct is listed in diagnostics[] as {source: vega-lite,
severity: unsupported, code: <id>} (without --json, also as an
'Unsupported: <id>: <message>' line on standard error); the message gives
file, line, column, and JSON pointer. With --strict the first one fails
with unsupported-feature.
vl-mark-<type>
A mark that is not drawn, for example vl-mark-geoshape; the view is
drawn without marks.
vl-channel-geo
A longitude or latitude channel.
vl-channel-url
A url channel on a mark other than image: Vega-Lite ignores it there,
and so does the chart.
svg-image-unresolved
Warning: the url of an image mark cannot be drawn (the file is missing,
remote, of an unknown type, or embeds itself). Reported once, with the
reason; nothing is drawn. With --strict it fails with
unsupported-feature, naming the chart and the url.
image-fragment-invalid and image-page-out-of-range (a #page= that no
page matches) are reported and fail with --strict the same way;
svg-image-too-large is a picture beyond the pixel budget, and a url the
file-access mode denies is image-access-denied.
vl-data-remote-url
A url with a scheme other than a local file: URI (http, https, data, a
file: URI with a host), or a network path: never fetched, empty dataset.
vl-data-geo
Geographic data (sphere, graticule, topojson).
vl-projection
A projection.
vl-param-selection-layer
A top-level selection param of a layered view that has two or more
layers: Vega-Lite compiles duplicate signals that Vega rejects; the
selection is applied as empty (declare it in one layer, or name the
layer in views).
vl-param-selection-id
A point selection with no fields or encodings and an initial value: it
selects rows by identity, which is not modeled; the selection is applied
as empty.
vl-param-selection-animation
An animation selection (on: timer): drawn in its initial state, without
the animation.
vl-param-selection-projection
Warning: a selection cannot be projected over a channel (the view has no
field on it, or its field is aggregated), an interval selection is
initialized with a key that is not a channel, a selection used as a
scale domain or a bin extent names no usable field and projects several
(the first is used), or a selection bound to the scales projects a
channel without a continuous scale.
vl-param-variable
A variable param of a nested view (a layer or a composition): Vega-Lite
declares no signal for it, so it is ignored and an expression that reads
it sees null (Vega fails).
vl-param-unknown
Warning: the fragment of a link that embeds the chart
(chart.vl.json#param.nope=1) sets a param the specification does not
declare; the chart is drawn without it. --param of the command line is a
vega-lite-error for the same mistake. --strict does not fail on it. A
value that is not usable (a JSON array that is cut short) is
image-fragment-invalid and the chart is not drawn.
vl-transform-lookup-param
A lookup transform whose from is a param (the data of a selection): it
needs the final table of another view filtered by the selection, which
is not supported yet; the transform is not applied.
vl-expr-ref
An {"expr": ...} where Vega-Lite's schema allows none (a width or
height, or anywhere in a selection, for example), or in a place with no
row that reads datum.
vl-param-extent-static
Warning: an {"expr": ...} at a place that is fixed before the data is
read (a title, a configuration value, an axis or legend property) reads
the param that an extent transform computes; the param is null there.
The transforms that follow the extent, bin.extent, and scale.domain see
its value.
vl-expr-function-<name>
An expression function outside the supported 113, for example
vl-expr-function-now (also the sampling functions random, sampleNormal,
sampleLogNormal and sampleUniform): the call evaluates to null.
vl-guide-encode
axis.encode or legend.encode.
vl-offset-position
An xOffset or yOffset that has no nominal or ordinal x or y channel (or
a temporal one with a time unit that can hold it) to nest in: the offset
is ignored.
vl-offset-ranged
A temporal or binned xOffset or yOffset of a bar or area, or a
continuous one whose position has a time unit or an x2 or y2 channel (an
unbinned quantitative offset of a bar or area with a nominal or ordinal
position is drawn as a ranged offset): the offset is ignored.
vl-scale-invalid-value
An entry of config.scale.invalid that is neither "zero-or-min" nor an
object with a number or text value (null, a boolean, a list; an
expression reference is vl-expr-ref instead): the channel is treated as
without an entry, so the invalid mode of the mark handles its invalid
rows.
vl-shape-path-invalid
Warning: a shape that is neither a symbol name nor SVG path data that
parses (for example M0,0L): a circle is drawn; a path with no command
draws nothing. A valid SVG path is drawn, scaled by the symbol size as
Vega does (a path of 1 unit is half the symbol side).
vl-scale-<type>
A scale type that is not supported, for example vl-scale-identity.
vl-type-geojson
The geojson field type.
vl-unknown-property
Warning: a property Vega-Lite does not define for that object.
vl-schema-version
Warning: a $schema that is not version 5 or 6; version 6 defaults are
used.
vl-layout-fit-step
Warning: autosize fit together with a step size; the fit is dropped for
that dimension.
vl-scale-domain-raw
Warning: the value of a param used as a scale domain (or a domainRaw) is
not an array of at least two numbers or dates (one value for a band,
point, or ordinal scale); the scale keeps its own domain.
vl-composition-property-ignored
Warning: a width, height, padding, config, or similar property of a
composition that only the top-level view decides.
vl-text-missing-glyph
Warning: text with characters that neither the font nor the bundled
fallback fonts have a glyph for (for example a private-use or CJK
character); the font's missing-glyph box is drawn. Reported at the text
mark, or with no location for axis labels, legends, and titles.
- Warnings have the code vega-lite-warning and carry the vl-* identifier at
the start of the message text, after the location. Errors: vega-lite-error
(invalid specification, a data file that is missing or refused, a chart
that cannot be drawn), budget-exceeded (a library limit), corrupt-input (a
specification longer than 4194304 characters), and size-limit (a chart
laid out beyond 8192 pixels on a side).
- See the Vega-Lite section of the Vega-Lite user guide for the complete
list of identifiers.
Known differences from Vega-Lite:
- The picture is static: no interaction, and tooltips are omitted. A
selection or a param is drawn in its initial state, as vega-embed paints
it before any event; a date in a selection value is read in UTC. The brush
of an initial interval selection is drawn (nothing is made for a brush
with no extent, where Vega-Lite makes a zero-size rectangle), and bind:
scales applies where Vega-Lite applies it to a still chart.
- A schema of version 5 is drawn with the version 6 defaults (a view is 300
by 300 pixels by default, for example).
- Text is measured with the bundled fonts, so labels, legends, and facet
headers can differ from a browser by a few pixels. A character the
Liberation fonts lack is drawn from the bundled Noto fonts, never from an
installed font, so the result does not depend on the machine.
- Dates are always UTC; nothing is read from the network; data files are
read relative to the specification's folder, under --file-access.
- A chart can be drawn inside an SVG diagram with <image
href="chart.vl.json" .../> (see 'canvasnet help svg'); it keeps its own
background there, and #param.<name>=<value> in the href sets a param of
the chart the way --param does.
- Pictures of an image mark are loaded when the chart is drawn, relative to
the chart's folder, and the chart is laid out without them: the size of a
picture never changes the size of the chart. A raster keeps its pixels as
scene units (at --scale 2 it covers twice the pixels); a model, an SVG
file, a PDF page, or a chart without a width and height of the mark is
drawn 256 units wide and high; a picture that a width and a height fit is
fitted inside the box and centered when its aspect ratio differs (aspect
false stretches it). One picture that many rows show is loaded once. At
most 256 different pictures are loaded; beyond that the chart fails with
budget-exceeded.
- Color schemes are interpolated piecewise in sRGB, not taken from the
d3-scale-chromatic tables.
- labelExpr and the other expressions have format(value, specifier)
(d3-format), timeFormat() and utcFormat() (d3-time-format); an invalid
specifier is a render error. config.legend.labelExpr is not read, as in
Vega-Lite 6.
- Composite marks (boxplot, errorbar, errorband) group by the bin, time
unit, and aggregate of their channels as Vega-Lite does; the one
difference is that the box of a box plot over a bin spans the whole bin,
where Vega-Lite 6.5 draws it from the middle of the bin to its end.
- A mark with invalid: "show" (or null) draws a row whose value is not a
number at zero (or at the first value of the domain), and an entry of
config.scale.invalid ("zero-or-min", or a number or text value) does the
same for its channel whatever the invalid mode is (a value is the output
of the property as it is, not scaled); a stacked row of a null stays in
its slot, and a stacked channel ignores its config.scale.invalid entry. An
invalid custom SVG path shape is a warning and a circle, where Vega fails.
- The distribution functions of expressions are pure and follow
vega-statistics (the cumulative normal is the approximation of West, the
quantile uses an inverse error function approximation); the sampling
functions are not available, so an expression gives the same result on
every run. A symbol legend with a clipHeight clips its symbols to entries
of that height; a gradient legend ignores it, as Vega does.
- The statistical transforms follow Vega: the groups of regression, loess,
density, and quantile are keyed by the text of the group values, a density
counts every row (a null reads as 0, a text that is not a number makes the
density NaN), a shared density samples a uniform grid (Vega-Lite's
default), and a pivot gives no value (not 0) for a combination without
rows. A regression with params: true gives one row of keys, coef, and
rSquared; the curve of a date is sampled in milliseconds; the order of a
poly regression is an integer from 0 to 64 and the bandwidth of a loess is
from 0 to 1. The extent transform writes its [min, max] into the param
while the data is read.
- A shared legend shows the symbols of the first layer.
- Compositions drop more properties than Vega-Lite does; each is reported as
a warning.
- Delimited text is not type-inferred (as in Vega): cells stay strings
unless format.parse says otherwise.
- A line feed inside title text splits the title into lines, which Vega
itself does not do.
- Compared with vega-embed: no actions menu, no signals, no renderer choice,
and no config or datasets injection from the command line.

commands.name: vsdx
commands.description: Each drawing page is a page, drawn as an image.

options.name: --page
options.description: The page to draw, counted from 1 (default 1).

options.name: --all-pages
options.description:
Draw every page; for a drawing of more than one page the output must
contain {page} or be a directory.

options.name: --dpi
options.description:
Resolution in dots per inch (default 96, a whole number above 0 and at
most 2400).

options.name: --background
options.description: The color transparency is flattened over (white by default).

options.name: --strict
options.description:
Fail with unsupported-feature instead of drawing with an approximation.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- Each report is listed in diagnostics[] as {source: vsdx, severity:
unsupported, code: <token>} (without --json, also as an 'Unsupported:
<token>: <message>' line on standard error), once per distinct feature per
page. With --strict the first report fails with unsupported-feature.
vsdx-themed-color
A themed color was drawn neutral gray.
vsdx-geometry-spline-approximated
A curve was approximated by a polyline.
vsdx-geometry-row-<Type>
A geometry row was skipped.
Known differences from Visio:
- The approximations listed above, in particular neutral gray for themed
colors that cannot be resolved.
- Fonts that are not embedded come from the machine, so text can differ
between machines.
